recipes.name: Roasted Pecan Banana Bread Loaves
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup light butter, at room temperature

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C). Spread pecans onto a rimmed baking sheet.

Toast in the preheated oven until golden brown and fragrant, about 45 minutes. Watch pecans carefully as they bake, as they burn quickly. Remove from the oven and cool to room temperature, about 15 minutes.
Increase the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Spray two 4-compartment mini loaf pans with cooking spray.
Combine toasted pecans, flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.

Mix bananas, sugar, butter, eggs, lemon juice, vanilla, and coconut extract in a large bowl with a fork or an electric mixer on low speed. Stir in flour mixture until incorporated. Pour batter into the prepared loaf pans, filling each one about 3/4 full.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 30 minutes. Let cool in the pans for 5 minutes before turning out onto a rack to finish cooling.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Pecan Banana Bread Loaves
raw_recipe.description: These mini banana nut bread loaves are made with buttery pecans for added texture and a touch of coconut extract to amplify the banana flavor.

review.reviewBody: I used whole wheat flour, I cut the sugar back to a half cup (my bananas were REALLY ripe so I really didn't need that much sugar) and used free-range eggs. She wasn't kidding about the coconut extract really being the money flavor in these muffins. Holy frijoles, was that GOOD! And I'll tell you, using whole wheat flour and cutting back on the sugar didn't affect the flavor AT ALL. NOTE: I got 12 medium-large muffins out of this recipe. 350* for 20 minutes was just right for muffins. If you want to avoid a rubbery loaf/muffin, I suggest you wisk together the dry ingredients in one bowl, then wisk together all the wet and lightly fold the wet ingredients into the dry. This way, you don't overwork your ingredients and don't end up with a "rubbery" muffin.

I made this recipe with a few substitutions based on ingredients I had on hand and it came out delicious! I used almond extract in place of coconut, turbinado sugar rather than white, unbleached AP flour, and regular unsalted butter. I made muffins which cooked perfectly in 30 minutes! I also toasted the well chopped pecans for only 10 minutes in toaster oven and they are delicious.

I didn't have coconut extract, so I used half a can of coconut milk instead, and I substituted coconut oil for the butter. (Next time I'll cut back on that, as it seemed a little oily.) I reduced the sugar to 1 3/4 cups (for a double recipe) and toasted the pecans on the stovetop. The result was delicious! It took a long time to cook, though. I baked it in muffin form, and when the muffins were still gooey inside after about 1/2 an hour in the oven, I turned up the heat to 350. It still took another 10-15 minutes before they were done. Next time I'll just use the higher temperature from the beginning.

Yes! I toasted wal-nuts 1/4 cup with the pecans. I used almond extract in place of the coconut extract. I used orange juice squeezed fresh( in place of the lemon juice). I also added 1/ 2 tsp cinnamon. It was the most flavorful Banana Nut Bread I have ever had!!

Sitting here munching on it with a cup of tea!! Absolute delicious, I made one loaf in a 9x5 tin and baked for about 45 mins covering the last part so it didn’t brown too much. I used candied pecans instead. I’ll definitely make this again.

I never made banana nut bread in my life this recipe had 5 stars and decided to try it , I doubled the recipe and used 1/2 coconut and 1/2 butter and i mixed the toasted pecans with the wet ingredients instead of dry it still came out really good
My sisters loved this and requested for more! Used the mini loaves pan, added 3/4 c of sweetened coconut flakes and reduced sugar to 1/2 c.
Added 1/2 cup instant oats & turned out great!
Very tasty and fluffy, only had one cup of banana and would probably cut back on the sugar next time.

It was simple and easy. I altered the recipe and used shredded coconut about 1/4 cup as a substitute for the coconut extract that I didn't have. Along with substituting butter with margarine. Omitted the pecans and used a muffin instead of a loaf pan. Baking now today 12/15/2019. Waiting on results. For now, the star rating is 4 until the baking is done.

Update on the 12/15/19 post. As of 12/16/2019, everything is done and I am able to add some pictures. Lest I not forget the rating goes to 5.

Forgot to include that I used unbleached flour and organic sugar. I will do this recipe and try some other flours and sugars.

My daughter and I experiment with this recipe, adapting it to our way of eating, and really like it. We use rice flour, 1 cup of agave for sweetener, coconut oil and sometimes ghee, no coconut extract. Our family loves it!

I have made this recipe many times and every one really likes it. I use 1l2 butter and 1/2 coconut oil. Instead of lemon juice, I use milk. I also cut the sugar in half, as my bananas are really ripe.
I used all vanilla extract because I'm allergic to coconut.
Love it. Simply delicious. Used coconut oil instead of coconut flavoring.
I thought it was a little dry. Even added a caramel sauce on the top to help, but was just ok
Delicious!

I’ve made this over and over for my family and they love it!!! It is so incredibly moist and flavorful. I only added more walnuts. It’s no better satisfaction than to see your family eating the bread right out of the pan with a fork. If I go too long without making it I hear about it...lol
Nice texture. I didn't have any extracts the first time I made it and only used 1/2 cup sugar (on purpose). Next time, get the extracts and try 2/3 cup of sugar.

3.19.19 My mini loaf pans are 3-1/2”x 6”, I baked for 35 minutes at 350ºF, and ended up with three mini loaves of banana bread. There were some different ingredients in this recipe not typically found in banana bread, and that piqued my curiosity. I followed this recipe to the letter except for using unsalted butter instead of light butter. The loaves baked up pretty much flat on the top rather than a slight dome that you find on most banana bread, but that’s not a negative, just different. You taste the hint of coconut flavor (I loved that), it’s pleasantly sweet, super moist, and almost more like a cake than a quick/sweet bread. So you can call it cake or you can call it bread, but to me, all that really matters is how it tastes, and that is lip-smacking GOOD!!
The only thing I did differently was add a few pecan halves on top so people would know it contains nuts
